want.now.why: SOV: object খাসি and infinitive শিখতে come first, then the door চাই, whose ending alone carries person and present. No auxiliary, no gender.

want.past.why: Past fuses into the door: চেয়েছিলাম is the everyday 'I wanted'; চাইছিলাম ('was wanting') is common for a wish that lingered.

want.neg.why: না comes after the verb and ends the sentence (চাই না), the mirror image of Hindi नहीं चाहता; the door keeps its present ending.

want.q.why: কি slots in right after the subject, not at the front, and nothing inverts. চাও is the informal তুমি ending of চাওয়া.

decline.now.why: A present can't is 'am not managing' (পারছি না). After কারণ the doer is আমাকে, and a one-off duty takes future হবে even when said now.

decline.past.why: Past negation fuses into one word: পারিনি, present stem plus নি; পারলাম না is also heard for a just-missed event. হয়েছিল carries the past on the duty.

decline.fut.why: CAN has a plain future পারব with না after it. The second half is word for word the same as the 'now' sentence: হবে was future all along.

decline.although.why: The যদিও clause comes first and তবু ('still') opens the main one, flipping English order. Both halves are in future, as for a plan.

like.now.why: The liker is genitive আমার and the coffee 'feels good' (ভালো লাগে); লাগে agrees with the coffee, so nothing here marks me.

like.neg.why: না is simply tacked on after লাগে; there is no auxiliary to split and nothing moves, unlike English 'don't like'.

like.she.why: Only আমার becomes ওর; ও/ওর means he or she alike, and লাগে stays put because it agrees with the coffee, not with her.

like.q.why: কি follows the informal genitive তোমার; the verb লাগে is untouched, so the question is marked only by কি and rising pitch.

go.habit.why: বাজারে is market + locative -এ, so 'to the market' is one word. Time রোজ comes before place, and যাই closes with present in its ending.

go.prog.why: The progressive is fused into one word: যাচ্ছি, with -চ্ছ- marking 'ongoing'. No separate 'am'; only the ending changed from যাই.

go.past.why: কাল is both yesterday and tomorrow; only the verb decides. For a specific earlier day speakers say গেছিলাম (written গিয়েছিলাম), not গেলাম.

go.fut.why: One word যাব fuses go and will. Same কাল as in 'yesterday': swap গেছিলাম for যাব and the day flips.

go.neg.why: না follows the verb (যাচ্ছি না) instead of preceding it, and closes the sentence; the progressive ending stays intact.

live.now.why: No perfect needed: present progressive থাকছি plus ধরে ('holding') on the duration. Many speakers just say এখানে আছি, 'I am here'.

live.past.why: A finished stay drops ধরে and uses ছিলাম, 'I was', for lived; থাকতাম would mean 'used to live' instead.

live.fut.why: Bengali turns it round: 'my three years of living here will be done'. Verbal noun থাকার, and the future sits on হয়ে যাবে.

live.q.why: কতদিন ধরে ('since how many days') stays in place before the verb rather than fronting; nothing inverts. তুমি এখানে কতদিন আছ? is just as common.

if.real.why: যদি sits after the subject, and the if-verb পাই is plain present ('get time'). তাহলে opens the result, whose subject is dropped: যাব shows it.

if.unreal.why: Unreal uses the -তাম form in both halves, পেতাম ... যেতাম, with no separate 'would'. Casual speech drops যদি: সময় পেলে ঘুরতে যেতাম.

if.past.why: The verbs are identical to the unreal sentence: -তাম covers both. Only তখন ('back then') tells you the chance is gone.
